title: Protostar L1527
caption: The protostar L1527, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: LDN 1527 · constellation Taurus · about 460 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, and STScI, J. DePasquale (STScI)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Glowing cavities open above and below a young star in this Webb infrared view, their edges shining orange and blue. The star is the protostar L1527, buried in a cloud of gas and dust that it is feeding on as it grows. Material thrown out by the star has cleared these cavities.

In the upper central region, bubble-like shapes mark stellar 'burps', sporadic ejections from the young star. Webb also picks out filaments of molecular hydrogen that has been shocked by earlier outbursts, a record of the star's restless past.

The shapes are curiously uneven. The cavity edges at upper left and lower right look straight, while those at upper right and lower left curve. The colors carry information too. The lower right region looks blue because there is less dust between it and Webb than in the orange regions above it. Working in infrared lets Webb look into the dusty cloud around the protostar.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.25 x 2.30 arcminutes) and distance (460 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.3 × 0.3 light-years. Its light set out about 460 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image comes from Webb's NIRCam. The shortest filter is shown in blue, a filter tracing PAH molecules in green, a molecular hydrogen filter in orange and another long-wavelength filter in red.
understand.eye: This is infrared light, invisible to the eye. The colors are assigned, and here they also hint at how much dust lies in front of each region.

explore: L1527 lies about 460 light-years away in the direction of the constellation Taurus. A protostar is a star still in the making, gathering mass from its surroundings before it begins to shine by nuclear fusion in its core.
alt: A young star's cloud with glowing cavities above and below it, their boundaries orange and blue, bubble-like shapes in the upper center and a bluer region at lower right.
